passage:
A town repaired the public clock in its square after years of silence. Some people said clocks were unnecessary because everyone had phones.
But when the clock began ringing again, residents noticed something. People looked up. Children asked about the tower. Older residents remembered meeting there before mobile phones.
The clock did not provide information people lacked. It provided shared time in a shared place.
A phone tells time privately. A public clock tells time to everyone at once.
The town learned that some old tools remain useful not because they are needed for function, but because they create common experience.
